seo.title: TablePro vs MySQL Workbench: features and compatibility
seo.description: MySQL Workbench is Oracle’s free tool for MySQL, now rebuilt on MySQL Shell. TablePro covers MySQL and other engines on Mac, iPhone and iPad.

header.title: TablePro vs MySQL Workbench
header.lead: MySQL Workbench is Oracle’s tool for MySQL. Version {status.version} rebuilt it on MySQL Shell. Compare it with TablePro for MySQL, MariaDB and other databases.

tablepro: MySQL and MariaDB alongside other database types.
MySQL 8.0 connections; the new Workbench supports {cells.databases.version} and later.
An Intel Mac build or a free iPhone and iPad app.
competitor: Oracle’s own free tool for MySQL.
SQL notebooks with JavaScript and TypeScript.
MySQL Enterprise Backup integration or guided HeatWave migration.

glance.intro: MySQL Workbench {status.version} is a new generation built on MySQL Shell, and Oracle says not every feature of Workbench 8.0 is in it yet. Version {cells.workbench8.version} is the last release of Workbench 8.0.

notebooks.label: SQL notebooks
notebooks.tablepro: Not available. SQL runs in editor tabs, with a query history

administration.label: Server administration
administration.tablepro: Free in the Mac app: Users & Roles with grants down to a column, and a Server Dashboard that cancels a query or ends a session

enterpriseBackup.label: Backups
enterpriseBackup.tablepro: Free: Backup Dump and Restore Dump run mysqldump and mysql, which you install

workbench8.label: Previous generation
workbench8.tablepro: One version line, updated in the app or through Homebrew

items.text: MySQL Workbench is Oracle’s own tool for MySQL, free and open source under the GPL.
Its SQL notebooks mix queries, results and notes in one document, and run JavaScript and TypeScript as well as SQL.
With MySQL Enterprise Backup, it creates, schedules and restores full and incremental backups.
The HeatWave Migration Assistant guides a move to MySQL HeatWave on OCI.
One client covers MySQL, MariaDB and other engines, such as PostgreSQL, SQL Server, SQLite and Redis. See the <link>supported databases</link>.
TablePro connects to MySQL 8.0 servers too. Oracle supports MySQL {cells.databases.version} and later in the new Workbench, and says older versions may work.
It runs on Intel Macs as well as Apple silicon, with a separate build for each. The new Workbench’s Mac download is for Apple silicon only.
<link>Backup Dump</link> runs mysqldump and Restore Dump runs mysql, so backups need no MySQL Enterprise Backup. Both are free.
The <link>AI assistant and the MCP server</link> are free in the Mac app, with the AI provider you choose.
A free <link>iPhone and iPad app</link> connects to MySQL and MariaDB, with no in-app purchases.
There are no notebooks, and MySQL connections run SQL, not JavaScript or TypeScript.
TablePro has no MySQL Enterprise Backup integration and no migration assistant for MySQL HeatWave.
It connects to MySQL over TCP only, not through a local socket file.
Some features are paid. Starter adds features such as {starterExamples}, while MySQL Workbench is free.

switching.intro: TablePro has no importer for MySQL Workbench. Add each connection by hand: fill in the connection form, or paste a URL that starts with mysql:// into <ui>File > Import > Import from URL…</ui>
after: Set up an SSH tunnel on the connection’s <ui>Network</ui> tab, with jump hosts if you need them.
If a project keeps its database settings in a file such as .env or wp-config.php, <ui>File > Import > Open Project Folder…</ui> reads them and opens the connection form filled in.
Passwords go into the macOS Keychain, and query history starts fresh in TablePro.

faq.question: Is MySQL Workbench 8.0 still maintained?
faq.answer: No. Oracle says Workbench 8.0 has reached end of life and will have no new releases, and {cells.workbench8.version} is its last version. Oracle asks its users to move to MySQL Workbench {status.version}, a rebuild that does not yet have every feature of Workbench 8.0.

faq.question: Does TablePro work with MySQL 8.0 and MariaDB?
faq.answer: Yes. TablePro connects to MySQL 8.0, to later versions and to MariaDB through the same driver. Oracle supports MySQL {cells.databases.version} and later in the new Workbench, and says older versions may work. <link>Read about MySQL in TablePro</link>.

faq.question: Does MySQL Workbench run on an Intel Mac?
faq.answer: The Mac download of version {status.version} is for Apple silicon only. TablePro has a separate build for Intel Macs. <link>Download TablePro</link>.
